text: A workshop produces tables and chairs. Let x1 be the number of tables produced and x2 the number of chairs produced. Both quantities may take any nonnegative real value, including fractional values. The profit per table is {objective_x1} EUR, and the profit per chair is {objective_x2} EUR. Producing each table requires {constraint_1_x1} h of labor and {constraint_2_x1} kg of wood. Producing each chair requires {constraint_1_x2} h of labor and {constraint_2_x2} kg of wood. At most {rhs_1} h of labor and {rhs_2} kg of wood are available. Determine the production quantities that maximize total profit.

A farm purchases two feed supplements, supplement A and supplement B. Let x1 be the amount of supplement A purchased, measured in kg, and x2 the amount of supplement B purchased, measured in kg. Both amounts may take any nonnegative real value, including fractional values. The cost per kg is {objective_x1} EUR for supplement A and {objective_x2} EUR for supplement B. Each kg of supplement A supplies {constraint_1_x1} g of nutrient P, and each kg of supplement B supplies {constraint_1_x2} g of nutrient P. The total amount purchased must supply at least {rhs_1} g of nutrient P. Each kg of supplement A supplies {constraint_2_x1} g of nutrient Q, and each kg of supplement B supplies {constraint_2_x2} g of nutrient Q. The total amount purchased must supply at least {rhs_2} g of nutrient Q. Determine the amounts of the two supplements to purchase to minimize total cost.
